skill.name: Draft a Commit
skill.description: Draft clear commit messages from staged Git changes without modifying the repository.
skill.summary: Review staged changes and draft an editable commit message with useful context.
skill.author: AbeJitsu

security_audit.summary: Manual review of SKILL.md found a prompt-only workflow for reviewing staged Git changes and drafting commit messages. The invalid-frontmatter scan limitation is not a security risk, and no prompt injection, data exfiltration, or repository-modifying behavior was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Manual review of SKILL.md shows a documentation-only skill that uses staged diffs to draft a message. The invalid frontmatter affected automated scanning but does not create a security risk.

low_findings.title: Unscanned file (invalid_frontmatter) — manual review required
low_findings.confidence_reasoning: Force-confirmed metadata/low static finding; AI false-positive verdict rejected.

content.value_statement: Staged changes can be difficult to summarize clearly. This skill reviews the staged diff and drafts an editable commit message that explains the change and its purpose.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged changes with git diff --cached.
Classifies changes such as features, fixes, documentation, and refactoring.
Drafts descriptive or conventional-style commit messages.
Includes optional context and file-change counts in the draft.
Handles empty staged changes by suggesting the next step.
Leaves staging and committing under user control.
limitations: It analyzes only changes that are already staged.
It infers intent from diffs and may need clarification for ambiguous changes.
It does not stage files, create commits, or modify the repository.
Its configuration defaults must be edited manually per project.

use_cases.title: Prepare a feature commit
use_cases.description: Turn staged implementation, tests, and documentation into a message that explains the delivered feature.

use_cases.title: Standardize team history
use_cases.description: Use conventional formatting to create consistent commit messages during team development.

use_cases.title: Document a maintenance change
use_cases.description: Describe a small fix or refactor with enough context for future maintainers.

prompt_templates.title: Draft my staged commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and draft a concise commit message.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the change purpose
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and draft a commit message that explains what changed and why.

prompt_templates.title: Use conventional commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and draft a conventional commit message with a clear type, scope, and rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Create a detailed release-ready message
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my staged changes. Draft a detailed commit message with the change summary, impact, rationale, and file counts.

output_examples.input: Staged changes add validation tests and update the API error handler.
output_examples.output:
Fix API error response validation

Return validated error objects and add coverage for malformed responses.

output_examples.input: Staged changes add setup documentation and link it from the README.
output_examples.output:
Document local setup process

Add a setup guide and connect it from the project README for new contributors.

best_practices: Stage only related changes before requesting a draft.
Review the drafted message and edit it to match the actual intent.
Use a consistent format that matches your project conventions.
anti_patterns: Do not use one draft to describe unrelated staged changes.
Do not accept inferred rationale without checking it against the work.
Do not expect the skill to stage files or create the commit.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Git commit?
faq.answer: No. It drafts a message for you to review and use yourself.

faq.question: Which changes does it review?
faq.answer: It reviews only changes that are already staged.

faq.question: Can I use conventional commit formatting?
faq.answer: Yes. Set the format option to conventional in the skill configuration.

faq.question: Can I edit the drafted message?
faq.answer: Yes. The draft is intended for review and editing before you commit.

faq.question: What happens when no files are staged?
faq.answer: The skill reports that no staged changes are available and suggests staging files first.

faq.question: Does it change repository files?
faq.answer: No. It does not stage files, commit changes, or modify the repository.
